{
  "title": "The Ten-Year Ledger",
  "world": "Cinematic Storybook Realism",
  "cold_open": "The clock in the lobby strikes midnight, and a single heavy door creaks open. Steam rises from the sidewalk.",
  "question": "Who is the man who returns the book every decade, his face as smooth as a river stone?",
  "journey": "For thirty years, the heavy leather volume arrived on the same Tuesday. It was always a man in a charcoal overcoat, his hands steady and gloved. He didn't speak to the librarians; he simply placed the book on the mahogany desk. Inside, the pages were filled with pressed wildflowers and meticulous notes in a handwriting that never changed. The ink was always fresh, the paper still carried the faint scent of cedar and old rain. He moved like a shadow through the stacks, a permanent fixture of the evening mist.",
  "discovery": "One night, a young clerk found a pressed violet between the pages. It wasn't a flower from the local fields. It was a species extinct for a century, its petals still vibrant, pulsing with a phantom color that defied the passage of time.",
  "emotional_turn": "The man arrived again, his face unchanged, but his hands trembled for the first time. He placed a small, rusted key inside the cover—a key to a house that had burned down before the library was even built.",
  "payoff": "He leaned in, whispering a name into the spine of the book. It was the name of the girl who first sat in this very chair, a century ago, dreaming of worlds she would never see. He finally closed his eyes.",
  "after_image": "The book sits on the desk, the key turning in a lock that no longer exists.",
  "hero_shot": "A single, vibrant violet petal rests on a page of perfectly preserved, golden-inked script."
}
